notes.title: Headers middleware: accessControlAllowOrigin
notes.text: `accessControlAllowOrigin` is deprecated. This field will be removed in future 2.x releases.

notes.title: Expose an Ingress on 80 and 443
notes.text: Define the default TLS configuration on the HTTPS entry point.

notes.title: InsecureSNI removal
notes.text: Since `v2.2.5` this global option has been removed, and you should not use it anymore.

notes.title: HostSNI rule matcher removal
notes.text: Since `v2.2.5` this rule has been removed for HTTP routers, and you should not use it anymore.

notes.title: X.509 CommonName Deprecation
notes.text: The deprecated, legacy behavior of treating the CommonName field on X.509 certificates as a host name when no Subject Alternative Names are present, is now disabled by default.

notes.title: K8S CrossNamespace
notes.text: In `v2.4.10`, the default value for `allowCrossNamespace` has been changed to `false`.

notes.title: K8S ExternalName Service
notes.text: In `v2.4.10`, by default, it is no longer authorized to reference Kubernetes ExternalName services.

notes.title: Headers middleware: ssl redirect options
notes.text: `sslRedirect`, `sslTemporaryRedirect`, `sslHost` and `sslForceHost` are deprecated in Traefik v2.5.

notes.title: Headers middleware: accessControlAllowOrigin
notes.text: `accessControlAllowOrigin` is no longer supported in Traefik v2.5.

notes.title: X.509 CommonName Deprecation Bis
notes.text: Following up on the deprecation started previously, as the `x509ignoreCN=0` value for the `GODEBUG` is deprecated in Go 1.17, the legacy behavior related to the CommonName field cannot be enabled at all anymore.

notes.title: Errors middleware
notes.text: In `v2.5.4`, when the errors service is configured with the `PassHostHeader` option to `true` (default), the forwarded Host header value is now set to the client request Host value and not `0.0.0.0`.

notes.title: TLS client authentication
notes.text: In `v2.8`, the `caOptional` option is deprecated as TLS client authentication is a server side option.

notes.title: Consul Enterprise Namespaces
notes.text: In `v2.8`, the `namespace` option of Consul and Consul Catalog providers is deprecated, please use the `namespaces` options instead.

notes.title: Traefik Pilot
notes.text: In `v2.8`, the `pilot.token` and `pilot.dashboard` options are deprecated.

notes.title: Traefik Pilot
notes.text: In `v2.9`, Traefik Pilot support has been removed.

notes.title: Nomad Namespace
notes.text: In `v2.10`, the `namespace` option of the Nomad provider is deprecated, please use the `namespaces` options instead.

notes.title: Kubernetes CRDs
notes.text: In `v2.10`, the Kubernetes CRDs API Group `traefik.containo.us` is deprecated, and its support will end starting with Traefik v3.

notes.title: Traefik Hub
notes.text: In `v2.10`, Traefik Hub configuration has been removed because Traefik Hub v2 doesn't require this configuration.

notes.title: IPWhiteList (HTTP)
notes.text: In `v2.11`, the `IPWhiteList` middleware is deprecated, please use the IPAllowList middleware instead.

notes.title: IPWhiteList (TCP)
notes.text: In `v2.11`, the `IPWhiteList` middleware is deprecated, please use the IPAllowList middleware instead.

notes.title: TLS CipherSuites
notes.text: > By default, cipher suites without ECDHE support are no longer offered by either clients or servers during pre-TLS 1.3 handshakes. Decision has been made to support ECDHE cipher suites only by default.

notes.title: Minimum TLS Version
notes.text: > By default, the minimum version offered by `crypto/tls` servers is now TLS 1.2 if not specified with config.MinimumVersion, > matching the behavior of crypto/tls clients.

notes.text: Starting with `v2.11.1` the following timeout options are deprecated: - `<entryPoint>.transport.respondingTimeouts.readTimeout` - `<entryPoint>.transport.respondingTimeouts.writeTimeout` - `<entryPoint>.transport.respondingTimeouts.idleTimeout` They have been replaced by: - `<entryPoint>.transport.r

notes.title: EntryPoint.Transport.RespondingTimeouts.TCP.LingeringTimeout
notes.text: Starting with `v2.11.1` a new `lingeringTimeout` entryPoints option has been introduced, with a default value of 2s. This change avoids Traefik instances with the default configuration hanging while waiting for bytes to be read on the connection.

notes.title: LingeringTimeout
notes.text: Starting with `v2.11.2` the `<entrypoint>.transport.respondingTimeouts.tcp.lingeringTimeout` introduced in `v2.11.1` has been removed.

notes.title: RespondingTimeouts.TCP and RespondingTimeouts.HTTP
notes.text: Starting with `v2.11.2` the `respondingTimeouts.tcp` and `respondingTimeouts.http` sections introduced in `v2.11.1` have been removed.

notes.title: EntryPoint.Transport.RespondingTimeouts.ReadTimeout
notes.text: Starting with `v2.11.2` the entryPoints `readTimeout` option default value changed to 60 seconds. The default value was previously set to zero, which means no timeout.

notes.title: Connection headers
notes.text: Before, Traefik removed any header listed in the Connection header just before forwarding the request to the backends. Now, Traefik removes the headers listed in the Connection header as soon as the request is handled.

notes.title: MultiPath TCP
notes.text: Since `v2.11.28`, the MultiPath TCP support introduced with `v2.11.26` has been removed.

notes.title: Encoded Characters in Request Path

notes.title: Encoded Characters Configuration Default Values
notes.text: Since `v2.11.35`, the options for encoded characters now have a `true` default value. This means that Traefik will not reject requests with a path containing a specific set of encoded characters by default.

notes.title: maxResponseBodySize configuration on ForwardAuth middleware
notes.text: The default value for this option is -1, which means there is no limit to the response body size.

notes.title: maxResponseBodySize configuration on HTTP provider
notes.text: The default value for this option is -1, which means there is no limit to the response body size.

notes.text: If `allowCrossNamespace` is set to `false` (the default) and a `Chain` middleware references a middleware in a different namespace from its own, the whole `Chain` is now rejected and an error is logged.

notes.text: Traefik does not implement the deprecated h2c upgrade mechanism, it only serves unencrypted HTTP/2 with prior knowledge.

notes.title: SwarmMode
notes.text: In v3, the provider Docker has been split into 2 providers: - Docker provider (without Swarm support) - Swarm provider (Swarm support only) This configuration is now unsupported and would prevent Traefik to start.

notes.title: TLS.CAOptional
notes.text: Docker provider `tls.CAOptional` option has been removed in v3, as TLS client authentication is a server side option (see https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls#ClientAuthType). ##### Remediation The `tls.caOptional` option should be removed from the Docker provider install configuration.

notes.title: Experimental Channel Resources (TLSRoute and TCPRoute)
notes.text: In v3, the Kubernetes Gateway API provider does not enable support for the experimental channel API resources by default.

notes.title: HTTP3
notes.text: In v3, HTTP/3 is no longer an experimental feature. It can be enabled on entry points without the associated `experimental.http3` option, which is now removed.

notes.title: Rancher v1 Provider
notes.text: In v3, the Rancher v1 provider has been removed because Rancher v1 is no longer actively maintained, and Rancher v2 is supported as a standard Kubernetes provider. This configuration is now unsupported and would prevent Traefik to start.

notes.title: Remediation
notes.text: Also, all Rancher provider related configuration should be removed from the install configuration.

notes.title: Marathon provider
notes.text: In v3, the Marathon provider has been removed. This configuration is now unsupported and would prevent Traefik to start.

notes.title: Remediation
notes.text: All Marathon provider related configuration should be removed from the install configuration.

notes.title: TLS.CAOptional
notes.text: HTTP provider `tls.CAOptional` option has been removed in v3, as TLS client authentication is a server side option (see https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls#ClientAuthType). ##### Remediation The `tls.caOptional` option should be removed from the HTTP provider install configuration.

notes.title: TLS.CAOptional
notes.text: ETCD provider `tls.CAOptional` option has been removed in v3, as TLS client authentication is a server side option (see https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls#ClientAuthType). ##### Remediation The `tls.caOptional` option should be removed from the ETCD provider install configuration.

notes.title: TLS.CAOptional
notes.text: Redis provider `tls.CAOptional` option has been removed in v3, as TLS client authentication is a server side option (see https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls#ClientAuthType). ##### Remediation The `tls.caOptional` option should be removed from the Redis provider install configuration.

notes.title: InfluxDB v1
notes.text: In v3, the InfluxDB v1 metrics provider has been removed. This configuration is now unsupported and would prevent Traefik to start.

notes.title: Remediation
notes.text: All InfluxDB v1 metrics provider related configuration should be removed from the install configuration.

notes.title: Pilot
notes.text: Traefik Pilot is no longer available since October 4th, 2022. In v2, Pilot configuration was deprecated and ineffective, it is now unsupported and would prevent Traefik to start.

notes.title: Remediation
notes.text: All Pilot related configuration should be removed from the install configuration.

notes.title: Kubernetes Ingress Path Matching
notes.text: In v3, the Kubernetes Ingress default path matching does not support regexes anymore.

notes.title: Remediation
notes.text: Two levels of remediation are possible: - Interpret the default path matcher `PathPrefix` with v2 syntax. - Adapt the path regex to be compatible with the Go regex syntax and change the default path matcher to use the `PathRegexp` matcher with the `traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.pathmatcher` a

notes.title: Internal Resources Observability
notes.text: In v3, observability for internal routers or services (e.g.: `ping@internal`) is disabled by default.

notes.title: Router Rule Matchers
notes.text: The default rule matchers syntax is now the v3 one, but for backward compatibility this can be configured. The v2 rule matchers syntax is deprecated and its support will be removed in the next major version.

notes.title: New V3 Syntax Notable Changes
notes.text: The `Headers` and `HeadersRegexp` matchers have been renamed to `Header` and `HeaderRegexp` respectively. `PathPrefix` no longer uses regular expressions to match path prefixes.

notes.title: Remediation
notes.text: ##### Configure the Default Syntax In Install Configuration The default rule matchers syntax is the expected syntax for any router that is not self opt-out from this default value. In v3, this is no longer supported and `PathRegexp` should be used instead.

notes.title: IPWhiteList
notes.text: In v3, we renamed the `IPWhiteList` middleware to `IPAllowList` without changing anything to the configuration.

notes.title: Deprecated Options Removal
notes.text: - The `tracing.datadog.globaltag` option has been removed. - The `tls.caOptional` option has been removed from the ForwardAuth middleware, as well as from the HTTP, Consul, Etcd, Redis, ZooKeeper, Consul Catalog, and Docker providers.

notes.text: The TCP LoadBalancer `terminationDelay` option has been deprecated.

notes.text: In v3, the Kubernetes Ingress API Group `networking.k8s.io/v1beta1` (removed since Kubernetes v1.22) support has been removed.
